exposure: Streamlined risk-adjusted cesarean section rate (RCSR) model
outcome: Model effectiveness (AUC, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, Brier score)
Consistency of hospital rankings (Kendall's tau coefficient)
cohort: The study utilized obstetric electronic health record (EHR) data from 56 provincial multicenter hospitals to calculate and compare risk-adjusted cesarean section rates.
finding: The streamlined risk-adjusted cesarean section rate model demonstrated substantial congruence with the traditional model in terms of performance evaluation and practical application within hospital settings.
mod_finding: The streamlined model for evaluating risk-adjusted cesarean section rates can effectively serve as a viable surrogate for the traditional model, providing a refined paradigm for assessing quality in obstetric healthcare services related to mode of birth.
cross-section timing: The study analyzed data spanning the years 2017, 2018, and 2019.
